learningObjectives: Read from and write to files using Python.
Handle runtime errors using try, except, else, and finally.
Build robust programs that respond safely to invalid operations.

activities.title: File Handling Flow
activities.instruction: Explore the safe workflow for working with a file.

content.concept: Python can open a file, perform read or write operations, and close it. The with statement is preferred because it manages cleanup automatically.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Creates a file object using a path and access mode.
Reads from or writes data to the opened file.
Creates a context manager that handles resource cleanup.
The file is closed automatically when the with block ends.

activities.title: File Mode Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the file mode that matches the required operation.

content.concept: The mode passed to open() determines how the file is accessed. Common modes include r for reading, w for writing, and a for appending.

choices: w → write and truncate existing content

activities.title: Exception Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the roles of try, except, else, and finally.

content.concept: Exception handling separates code that may fail from code that handles errors and cleanup.

descriptions: Contains code that may raise an exception.
Defines cleanup or code that should run regardless of success or failure.

content.concept: A robust exception-handling structure catches expected failures and can use finally for cleanup that must happen regardless of the result.
